label: The normal probability density function: f of x equals one divided by sigma times the square root of two pi, times e raised to the power minus the quantity x minus mu squared divided by two sigma squared
Standardizing an observation: z equals the observation x minus the mean mu, divided by the standard deviation sigma
The empirical rule: the probability of falling within one, two, and three standard deviations of the mean is approximately 68.3 percent, 95.4 percent, and 99.7 percent
The central 95 percent of the standard normal: the probability that Z lies between minus 1.96 and 1.96 equals 0.95
The normal-method reference interval: mean minus 1.96 times sigma up to mean plus 1.96 times sigma
